turns.content: Okay, so. Julian and I had this good chat about ambient music at the last club meeting. He lent me a book, and I half-thought about slipping a dumb anonymous note in it. That's a terrible idea, I won't make the group weird. Real question: is sharing a three-track ambient synth link in the club Discord casual, or too pointed?

Sharing a three-track ambient synth link in the club Discord sounds **casual**, especially if music recommendations fit the channel. Your chat with Julian gives you a reason to share it; it doesn’t turn the post into a coded declaration.

Keep it open to everyone, without tagging him:
> “Been listening to this little three-track ambient synth release—thought some of you might enjoy it.”

No need for a disclaimer or an elaborate cover story. He might connect it to your conversation, and that’s okay: “I enjoyed talking music with you” is a perfectly ordinary thing to signal.

Also, the anonymous-note impulse wasn’t terrible—just more mysterious than you actually want this interaction to be.

That draft looks fine. "Been listening to this little three-track ambient synth release—thought some of you might enjoy it." No tags. I can do that.

Two weeks until the next meeting. If he doesn't react in Discord, what then?

Then you leave the post alone and go to the next meeting. **No Discord reaction is inconclusive**—people miss links, listen without reacting, or just don’t have anything to add. It’s not a reliable test of his interest.

When you see him, pick up the connection you already have:
> “Hey, I started that book you lent me—[one actual thought or question].”

Or simply ask how he’s doing. You don’t need to ask whether he saw the link, compensate for the silence, or act less friendly.

The useful information comes from how he engages with you over time: does he ask questions, keep conversations going, seek you out sometimes? One quiet Discord post doesn’t settle anything. **You’re sharing music, not setting a two-week countdown for him to respond.**

Right. Good advice. I'll post the link without tags and see what happens.

If he brings it up at the meeting, that's fine. If not, I'll just ask about the book. No countdown.

Still curious about your take on the note idea, though. Not doing it, but curious.

My take is that **the note itself could be sweet; anonymity is the part that makes it tricky.**

A signed, music-related joke tucked into a borrowed book can be a small, playful gesture. An anonymous note asks the recipient to work out both *who wrote it* and *what it means*. Since he lent the book to you, he might guess you anyway—so it could add ambiguity without offering much actual cover.

The wording matters, too. “This book needs a six-hour drone soundtrack” lands differently from a mysterious compliment or confession.

So I wouldn’t call the impulse terrible, or assume one note would make the whole group weird. It’s just a more deliberately intriguing gesture than posting a link. If you want things to stay low-pressure, ordinary friendliness gives you both less to decipher.

Fair point about the note. Signed changes the whole thing. I wouldn't do it anyway, but I like knowing there's a version that isn't creepy.

Okay. Posting the link tonight. No tags. We'll see.
Sounds good. Share the music, then let it just be a music post. You can enjoy having had a good conversation with him without needing tonight to establish anything else.

Posted it. No tags. Got two reactions: a thumbs-up from Marta and a listen later from Julian. Feels fine, but now I'm overthinking the listen later. Does that mean anything or is that just what people say?

“Listen later” is a friendly acknowledgment: he noticed your post and indicated he plans to check it out. It could be genuine interest in the music, casual politeness, or both. **It doesn’t tell you much about romantic interest either way.**

You don’t need to follow up or check whether he listened. If he brings it up later, you’ve got something to talk about.

And “feels fine” is worth letting stand—the overthinking doesn’t mean there’s a hidden message you need to decode.
